title: Architecture
heading: Architecture
text: How the VRAM / DRAM / SSD tiers work, placement, modes, MoE fast path. Architecture This document describes how the VUGVA integration works inside llama.cpp, what each layer owns, and why the design looks the way it does.

title: Architecture
heading: 1. The three tiers
text: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐ hot │ VRAM (8 GB) ggml CUDA buffer │ cudaMalloc ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤ warm │ DRAM (32 GB pool) VUGVA_DRAM buffer type │ cudaHostAllocMapped │ (pinned, UVA-mapped) │ or pageable mmap ├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤ cold │ NVMe / page cache fallback host memory │ mmap, demand paging └──────────────────────────────────────────────┘ The warm tier is a first-class ggml buffer type ( VUGVA_DRAM ), not a compute backend. Its memory is allocated from the Rust VUGVA pool ( ggml-vugva/vugva-bridge.rs ↔︎ FFI vugva_pool_create/alloc/write/access/… ). The cold tier is ordinary pageable memory. VUGVA does not need an explicit SSD path: when the DRAM pool cannot hold everything, the allocation becomes pageable and the Linux page cache moves cold pages to NVMe on demand. This is why models larger than the pool still load.

title: Architecture
heading: 2. Placement (Algorithm 1)
text: Implemented in llama.cpp/src/llama-model.cpp in load_tensors() . Compute budget = free VRAM − reserve , where reserve = max(total_VRAM/8, 1 GiB) and can be overridden with VUGVA_RESERVE_MB ; VUGVA_VRAM_MB caps the budget too. Sum per-layer weight bytes from the GGUF metadata ( blk.N.* ), keeping two counters per layer: layer_bytes — the whole layer, layer_bytes_dense — the layer without sparse expert tensors. Compute the output layer cost. Tied models duplicate token_embd into the output buffer ( TENSOR_DUPLICATED ), so the embedding is counted there. Decide the MoE fast path (below). Fill the hot tier in order — output layer first, then layers i_gpu_start… — stopping at the first layer that does not fit. A contiguous block matters: every gap becomes a CPU↔︎GPU graph split per token. Tensors of layers marked warm are created in the warm buft list; the rest in the GPU list. Overrides (see §4) win over both. Placement is logged: [VUGVA] mode=zerocopy VRAM budget 6266 MiB (free 7290, reserve 1024) -> 23/65 layers + output on GPU, remainder -> VUGVA_DRAM tier

title: Architecture
heading: zerocopy
text: The warm tier is allocated with cudaHostAlloc(cudaHostAllocMapped | cudaHostAllocPortable) and the device alias is obtained with cudaHostGetDevicePointer . Under UVA the device pointer equals the host pointer, so a single tensor->data is valid on both sides. ggml-cuda accepts VUGVA_DRAM as a supported buffer type when VUGVA_ZEROCOPY=1 , so the scheduler assigns warm-layer nodes to the GPU. The kernels read the weights over PCIe directly. The CPU never touches the weights. Result: one graph split for the whole model, no H2D copies of weights. Cost: warm-tier reads are PCIe-bandwidth-bound. On a dense model this is roughly on par with CPU compute over RAM bandwidth; on a sparse MoE it wins decisively because only the active experts are read.

title: Architecture
heading: hybrid
text: Warm layers are computed by the CPU backend; only activations cross PCIe. This is the safe fallback when the warm tier does not fit in RAM. It produces many graph splits (one per CPU/GPU boundary), so expect lower throughput.

title: Architecture
heading: auto (default)
text: Picks zerocopy when all of the following hold: the GPU can map host memory ( ggml_backend_vugva_zerocopy_available() ), the estimated warm tier ( model − hot ) plus allocator slack fits MemAvailable with a max(4 GiB, warm/4) margin, the warm tier is below the pin cap (50 % of RAM by default). Otherwise it picks hybrid . The decision is logged.

title: Architecture
heading: 4. Tensor overrides and the MoE fast path
text: llama.cpp resolves each tensor's buffer type in llama_model_loader::create_tensor() in this order: explicit tensor_buft_overrides ( -ot , -cmoe , -ncmoe ), VUGVA auto-MoE override (new), the layer's buffer-type list (GPU list for hot layers, warm list otherwise).

title: Architecture
heading: Auto-MoE
text: If n_expert > 0 , no explicit overrides were given, and the model does not fit the VRAM budget, llama-model.cpp sets ml.auto_cpu_experts . The loader then routes tensors matching \.ffn_(up|down|gate|gate_up)_(ch|)exps to ggml_backend_cpu_buffer_type() . With mmap enabled, the CPU buffer type is backed by the GGUF mapping: zero copies , zero extra RAM, and only the active experts are touched per token. Shared experts ( ffn_*_shexp ) are not matched and stay hot. Why this is the right metric: a 35B MoE with 256 experts and 8 active touches ~1/32 of the expert stack per token. Streaming the full stack through PCIe or copying it into the DRAM pool is wasted work; paging in the active experts from the (usually cached) file is cheaper.

title: Architecture
heading: Explicit overrides
text: -cmoe overrides all expert tensors; -ncmoe N overrides the first N layers. In both cases the loader routes them to plain CPU memory (not the DRAM tier), avoiding a full copy of the expert stack into the pool. If a user asks for the DRAM tier explicitly ( -ot '…=VUGVA_DRAM' in upstream terms), that is honored instead.

title: Architecture
heading: 5. Why not a compute backend?
text: An earlier iteration registered VUGVA as a full scheduler backend for warm layers. The CUDA↔︎VUGVA boundary produced >1000 graph splits and crashed in sched_reserve on real models. Keeping VUGVA as a buffer type (plus UVA in zero-copy mode) gives the same memory behaviour with none of the scheduling cost. See IMPLEMENTATION.md for the post-mortem.

title: Architecture
heading: 6. Memory safety model
text: The warm tier can be pinned ( cudaMallocHost / cudaHostAllocMapped ) or pageable. Pinning is the only operation that can take the machine down, so it is gated in the allocator: pinned_total + request <= min(VUGVA_PIN_MB, 50% of RAM) request + pinned_total + 2 GiB <= MemAvailable If either check fails, the allocator refuses the pin and returns pageable memory. If a mapped allocation fails in zero-copy mode, VUGVA_ZEROCOPY is cleared so ggml-cuda stops accepting VUGVA_DRAM , and the scheduler falls back to the CPU. This makes over-commitment a performance problem, never a correctness or stability problem.

Useful to force the DRAM tier on small models VUGVA_RESERVE_MB integer MiB max(VRAM/8, 1024) VRAM kept free for KV cache, activations, CUDA context VUGVA_PIN_MB integer MiB 50 % of RAM maximum pinned warm-tier memory. Set higher only on a dedicated inference box VUGVA_DRAM_GB integer GB 32 (CMake) DRAM pool size at runtime VUGVA_AUTO_MOE 0 , 1 1 auto-route sparse experts to CPU/mmap when the model exceeds VRAM VUGVA_HOT_CACHE_MB integer MiB 0 VRAM cache for warm-tier weights; promote on use, LRU evict. title: Configuration
heading: Mode selection details
text: auto computes the warm-tier estimate as hot_est = free_VRAM − max(VRAM/8, 1 GiB) warm_est = (model_bytes − hot_est) * 1.2 + 64 MiB fits = warm_est + max(4 GiB, warm_est/4) <= MemAvailable && warm_est <= min(VUGVA_PIN_MB, RAM/2) and selects zerocopy iff fits , otherwise hybrid . With VUGVA_MODE=zerocopy forced, the same numbers are printed as a warning but the run still tries; the allocator refuses unsafe pins and degrades automatically.

title: Configuration
heading: CMake options
text: Option Default Effect VUGVA_ENABLE ON build the VUGVA backend VUGVA_DRAM_GB 32 compile-time DRAM pool default VUGVA_DIR /home/irfan/Desktop/VUGVA/vugva path to the VUGVA Rust crate GGML_CUDA ON CUDA compute backend GGML_CUDA_FA_QUANTS f16-f16 (+ cache) FlashAttention KV type combinations, e.g. q4_0-q4_0;q8_0-q8_0;f16-f16 GGML_CUDA_FA_QUANTS must include the KV types you intend to use. If -ctk q4_0 -ctv q4_0 is requested but q4_0-q4_0 was not compiled, CUDA FlashAttention has no kernel for that combination.

title: Configuration
heading: Kernel promotion ( VUGVA_HOT_CACHE_MB )
text: Static placement fills VRAM at load time. If VRAM is left over afterwards (conservative reserve, small VUGVA_VRAM_MB , room after the KV cache), that memory is dead weight. The tier cache uses it: VUGVA_HOT_CACHE_MB = 4096 VUGVA_STATS = 1 ./build/llama-cli -m model.gguf -ngl 99 ... warm-tier weight tensors are promoted to VRAM on first use and stay there, eviction is LRU under the byte budget, the cache is skipped when fewer than budget + 512 MiB of VRAM is free, because promoting into a full card thrashes (measured 1.20 → 0.60 t/s on a 27B) — the counter line below tells you which happened: [VUGVA] hot cache: 2048 MiB VRAM for warm-tier weights, promote-on-use + LRU eviction [VUGVA] tier stats: step 16 cache 394/2048 MiB | hit 3210 miss 214 promote 214 evict 0 promoted 394 MiB [VUGVA] hot cache ignored: only 961 MiB VRAM free, need 1024 MiB (static placement already uses the rest) A cache smaller than the per-token working set shows up as a large miss / evict count and slower decode — that is the honest failure mode, not a bug.

With a cache smaller than the working set, LRU evicts tensors the next step needs again and decode slows down — the counters make it obvious. 27B dense on a full card: VUGVA_HOT_CACHE_MB=512 is refused ( only 961 MiB VRAM free, need 1024 MiB ) and decode stays at 1.20 t/s. title: Benchmarks
heading: Cold-tier readahead ( VUGVA_PRELOAD )
text: The 35B MoE keeps 19.5 GB of experts in mmap'd CPU memory. With preload enabled, the background thread reported 4480/20707 MiB read ahead during a 48-token run (it stops when decode finishes, or when MemAvailable drops under 2 GiB). buff/cache grows; RSS does not. On a cold cache this is what turns the first pass from ~4 t/s into ~20-40 t/s.

title: Benchmarks
heading: Notes on measurement
text: The bundled CLI uses greedy sampling at --temp 0 , so repeated runs are identical; the numbers above use --temp 0.7 for readable output only. n_batch defaults to the prompt length; for long prompts set -b explicitly to keep prompt processing representative. The first run after a reboot is always slower for mmap'd weights; run each configuration twice and report the second.

title: Paper vs. code
heading: Paper vs. code
text: What the paper claims, what this code does, and the measured evidence. VUGVA Integration — Implementation Status Version: integration 0.2.0 · vendored llama.cpp b12119 ( 3de52ac3 , 2026-11-04) · VUGVA core 898e5e1 · paper DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21549808. See README.md (version matrix) and docs/ for user-facing docs and CHANGELOG.md for the history. This file previously described a plan to make VUGVA a compute backend in the llama.cpp scheduler ( supports_op=true , VUGVA claims every op, delegates to CUDA). That approach was tried and reverted: it produced >1000 graph splits and crashed in sched_reserve . The architecture below is what actually ships and is verified to run.

title: Paper vs. code
heading: Architecture (current)
text: VUGVA is a buffer type + memory tier manager , never a compute backend: GGUF file ──mmap──► VUGVA_DRAM buffer (warm tier, pool-accounted) │ ├─ hot: layers capped to free VRAM ─► CUDA0 buffer (VRAM) ├─ warm: everything else ─► VUGVA_DRAM (page cache / pinned) └─ cold: pool budget exceeded ─► SSD via page cache (mmap file) compute: CUDA runs the hot-tier layers; DRAM-tier weights are read directly by the CPU backend; llama.cpp's op_offload moves small/batched ops to CUDA. Key properties enforced in ggml-vugva/ggml-backend-vugva.cpp : Hook Behavior Why dev.supports_op true consulted only by weight_buft_supported() / select_buft() for weight placement . VUGVA is skipped as a scheduler backend in llama-context.cpp and has graph_compute = NULL , so it never executes ops. dev.get_buffer_type singleton per device llama.cpp compares buffer-type pointers ( is_default_buft ); a fresh instance per call broke the mmap zero-copy import and leaked. dev.get_host_buffer_type NULL otherwise llama.cpp's "avoid host buffers when using mmap" rule rewrites every VUGVA selection back to the plain CPU buffer. buft.alloc_buffer pool-accounted ( vugva_alloc ), cudaMallocHost storage, anonymous-mmap fallback

title: Paper vs. code
heading: Root causes fixed (the original broken state)
text: dev.supports_op returned false → every tensor rejected VUGVA_DRAM → weights fell through to the CUDA buffer type → one contiguous 19.9 GB cudaMalloc → OOM on the 8 GB card (the reported 35B failure). get_buffer_type allocated a new instance per call → is_default_buft never matched → mmap zero-copy import path was dead, plus a leak per call. make_gpu_buft_list() prepended VUGVA before CUDA → with (1) fixed, all weights (including -ngl layers) would have gone to DRAM, GPU idle. get_host_buffer_type() returned VUGVA's own buft → llama.cpp's mmap rule silently rewrote VUGVA selections to the CPU buffer. vugva_alloc failure (pool over budget) hard-failed the import → any model larger than the pool could not load at all. get_max_size() returned the 32 GB pool size (ggml uses it to chunk). tests/test_vugva.cpp built a std::vector from the negated return of llama_tokenize → std::length_error abort; it also forced n_gpu_layers=0 . CMake VUGVA_DRAM_GB was never wired into the backend (32 GB hardcoded), and the vugva_test target referenced by README/CI/CONTRIBUTING did not exist.

title: Paper vs. code
heading: Mode selection (llama-model.cpp, Algorithm-1 block)
text: Hot tier is a contiguous prefix of the requested layers (no holes, so no extra graph splits); the output layer is budgeted first and its tied embedding is counted (llama.cpp duplicates token_embd into the output buffer via TENSOR_DUPLICATED ). Tensors rewritten by --cpu-moe / -ncmoe ( tensor_buft_overrides ) are excluded from the hot-tier budget, so MoE models can keep all attention/SSM layers in VRAM. auto picks zerocopy only when the estimated warm tier fits in RAM with a 25%/4 GiB margin and stays below 50% of physical RAM; otherwise hybrid . Pinned allocations are capped (50% RAM, ≥2 GiB headroom, VUGVA_PIN_MB ) and a failed mapped allocation downgrades the run to hybrid instead of crashing. CPU-buft overrides ( --cpu-moe ) now use the plain CPU buffer (mmap-backed) instead of the VUGVA DRAM tier, avoiding a full copy of the expert stack.

title: Paper vs. code
heading: Paper vs. code: what is implemented, what is not
text: Three of the paper's mechanisms are implemented; one is partially implemented; one cannot be implemented in llama.cpp's execution model, and one is hardware gated. Everything below is reproduced on the reference machine (RTX 4060 8 GB, 29 GB RAM, NVMe, CUDA 13.2) with the numbers from docs/benchmarks.md . Paper claim Status Where Three-tier placement VRAM → DRAM → SSD (§3.1) implemented llama-model.cpp Algorithm 1 block, VUGVA_DRAM buft CPU-bypass data plane (§5.1) implemented (load + zero-copy reads) mapped pinned DRAM + UVA Algorithm 1: static placement into the hot tier implemented contiguous hot prefix, tied-embedding aware Algorithm 2: membrane-driven promotion / eviction implemented, opt-in VUGVA_HOT_CACHE_MB , tier manager below Algorithm 3: look-ahead prefetch partially implemented (cold tier) VUGVA_PRELOAD ; DRAM→VRAM pipelining deliberately absent GPUDirect Storage / IOMMU P2P cold tier not available on this hardware , probed at runtime ggml_backend_vugva_probe_cold_tier Paper's aggregate numbers (+54.8% throughput, −84.6% CPU) not reproduced ; different hardware and workload our own table below

title: Paper vs. code
heading: 1. Promotion / eviction of individual tensors — implemented (opt-in)
text: ggml-vugva/ggml-backend-vugva.cpp → Tier manager , called from llama_context::graph_compute ( tier_begin before the scheduler runs, tier_end after it is enqueued). On each decode step the graph's leaf weight tensors in VUGVA_DRAM are walked in graph (layer) order , which is the paper's look-ahead order. A miss allocates a VRAM slot, cudaMemcpyAsync s the tensor on a dedicated non-blocking stream and redirects tensor->data to it. A hit just bumps the LRU clock. Under budget pressure the least-recently-used slot is evicted and its tensor is pointed back at DRAM. Redirection is stable across steps : llama.cpp's CUDA-graph cache keys on source pointers, so moving a pointer every step would disable graph capture. Pointers change only on promotion and eviction. The cache refuses to enable when static placement already filled VRAM ( VUGVA_HOT_CACHE_MB > free VRAM ⇒ warn and stay static), because that pathological case is measurable: 27B, 17.4 GB, 512 MiB cache on a full card ran at 0.60 t/s vs 1.20 t/s static. With the gate, the same command reports hot cache ignored: only 961 MiB VRAM free and keeps 1.20 t/s. Measured effect (Qwen3.5 0.8B Q4_K_M, static budget forced to 100 MiB so only 8

title: Paper vs. code
heading: 2. Look-Ahead prefetch (Algorithm 3) — partially implemented
text: Implemented: cold-tier readahead. VUGVA_PRELOAD (default on) starts a background thread after the model loads and issues posix_fadvise(..., POSIX_FADV_WILLNEED) over the GGUF in 64 MiB chunks, 20 ms apart, stopping below 2 GiB of MemAvailable . It is the tier that actually reads from NVMe (the experts of a sparse MoE), it cannot pin memory (clean file pages are reclaimable), and it reports progress: [vugva] cold-tier prefetch: 4480/20707 MiB read ahead (22%) Not implemented: pipelined DRAM → VRAM weight streaming. This is not an omission that a few more lines would fix; the llama.cpp execution model excludes it: every kernel of a decode step is enqueued before any of them executes , so the weight pointer of layer k must be final at enqueue time. A copy issued "while layer k−1 computes" would therefore have to be part of the graph. a copy placed in the compute stream serializes with the kernels — that is exactly the hybrid path, measured at 0.85–1.2 t/s on the 27B versus 1.20 t/s for direct zero-copy reads. a copy on a second stream cannot be joined per layer, because ggml graphs have no event-wait op. The only way to overlap would be to make VUGVA a compute backend, which was tried

title: Paper vs. code
heading: 3. GPUDirect Storage / IOMMU P2P — not available here (probed, not assumed)
text: ggml_backend_vugva_probe_cold_tier() runs at startup and prints one line: [VUGVA] cold tier: cufile=yes pageable_access=yes host_ptr_p2p=yes iommu=no -> cold tier: OS page cache (GGUF mmap) libcufile is installed and the GPU can address host memory, but there is no IOMMU group for the NVMe controller, so a cuFile read would bounce through host memory — faster-looking code, same traffic. The probe only reports GDS eligible when libcufile, pageable access and an IOMMU are all present. Wiring cuFile into the loader is not implemented ; the cold tier is the page cache over the GGUF mapping, as stated.

title: Paper vs. code
heading: 4. The paper's measured numbers are not reproduced
text: The paper reports +54.8 % throughput and −84.6 % CPU on a non-NVLink multi-GPU cluster. This repository's measurements are single-GPU and are reported as such ( docs/benchmarks.md ); no number in this repo is derived from, or asserted to reproduce, the paper's aggregate figures. The CPU-bypass property that the paper quantifies is visible here as scheduler behaviour instead: graph splits = 1 and the CPU backend executing no layer, rather than as a percentage.

title: Paper vs. code
heading: Pool accounting
text: The Rust TieredPool ( /home/irfan/Desktop/VUGVA/vugva ) provides NUMA-local registration and bookkeeping ( vugva_alloc / vugva_dealloc / vugva_pool_info ); the ggml buffer owns the actual storage (mmap import or cudaMallocHost ). Pool size: cmake -DVUGVA_DRAM_GB=N , runtime override VUGVA_DRAM_GB=N . Note: the pool attempts a whole-range cuMemHostRegister at creation; on a 32 GB machine registering 32 GB fails harmlessly (bookkeeping still works).

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Troubleshooting
text: Slow first pass, pin refusals, KV cache types, graph splits. Troubleshooting

title: Troubleshooting
heading: The run is extremely slow on the first pass, then speeds up
text: Expected for mmap'd or pageable weights. The first pass faults pages in from NVMe; the Linux page cache keeps them afterwards. If the model is larger than RAM minus the desktop, the cache cannot hold it and every pass is disk-bound. Options: free up RAM (close browsers/IDEs), use a smaller quant, on a dedicated box, raise VUGVA_PIN_MB so the warm tier is pinned.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: [VUGVA] refusing to pin ... — using pageable DRAM instead
text: The pin cap (50 % of RAM, ≥ 2 GiB headroom) was hit. This is a safety feature , not a failure: the run continues with pageable memory and, in zero-copy mode, automatically switches to hybrid. If the machine is dedicated to inference, raise the cap explicitly: VUGVA_PIN_MB = 24000 ./build/llama-cli ... Never set it to the full RAM size; leave room for the page cache and the OS.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: [VUGVA] zero-copy allocation failed — disabling zero-copy
text: The GPU could not map a host allocation (driver/OOM). The scheduler degrades to the CPU backend for warm layers. Check nvidia-smi and available RAM. A reboot clears stale pinned allocations from killed processes.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: KV cache type error / -ctk q4_0 fails
text: Quantized KV needs a FlashAttention kernel compiled for that combination. Set it at configure time, e.g.: cmake -B build -DGGML_CUDA = ON \ -DGGML_CUDA_FA_QUANTS = "f16-f16;q8_0-q8_0;q4_0-q4_0" -fa on is enabled automatically by the CLI when a non-F16 KV type is requested.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: sched_reserve: graph splits is huge (50–120)
text: Warm layers are being computed by the CPU ( hybrid ). Every CPU/GPU boundary is a split. Compare with VUGVA_MODE=zerocopy , which normally reports graph splits = 1 . A large split count is expected in hybrid mode; it is not an error.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: GPU shows almost no VRAM used on a MoE model
text: That is the MoE fast path working: attention/SSM stays hot (~1.3 GB for a 35B), the sparse experts live in mmap'd CPU memory. Check the log: [VUGVA] MoE fast path: sparse experts -> CPU/mmap, attention/SSM stays hot in VRAM load_tensors: CPU_Mapped model buffer size = 19486.84 MiB Disable with VUGVA_AUTO_MOE=0 to restore whole-layer placement.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Model loads but output is garbage
text: Confirm the same prompt/seed reproduces with VUGVA_VRAM_MB=100 VUGVA_MODE=zerocopy (forced tier) vs. full GPU. If the forced tier matches the full-GPU text, the tiering data path is correct. With greedy sampling ( --temp 0 ) small numerical differences can push a model into a repetition loop; try --temp 0.7 --repeat-penalty 1.1 . The 0.8B tests in docs/benchmarks.md produce identical text in both modes.

title: Troubleshooting
heading: unable to load model / OOM at load
text: Check free RAM ( free -g ) and swapon --show . A previous killed process can leave swap full; a reboot or swapoff -a && swapon -a (root) clears it. The warm tier allocation is visible in the load log; if it is near your RAM size, let auto choose hybrid or lower VUGVA_DRAM_GB .

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Updating llama.cpp
text: The vendored source is a plain directory. To move to a new upstream snapshot: # the upstream git history is kept outside the tree git --git-dir = ../llama-cpp-upstream.git fetch origin master git --git-dir = ../llama-cpp-upstream.git diff < old > .. < new > -- \ src/llama-model.cpp src/llama-model-loader.cpp \ ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu examples/simple/simple.cpp Re-apply the VUGVA hunks (they are localized: placement block, loader override hook, CUDA supports_buft , CLI), rebuild, and record the new commit in the README version matrix. Keep the integration tag up to date ( llama.cpp-b<build>-<shortsha> ).

title: Troubleshooting
heading: Diagnostic commands
text: # what placement happened? VUGVA_MODE = auto ./build/llama-cli ... 2 >& 1 | grep -E "VUGVA|buffer size|graph splits" # scheduler detail GGML_SCHED_DEBUG = 1 ./build/llama-cli ... 2 >& 1 | head -100 # VRAM and RAM nvidia-smi --query-gpu = memory.used,memory.free --format = csv free -m ; swapon --show
